in_hebrew.name: עוקטביאן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עוקטביאן היא הגרסה הלטינית של השם היווני 'אקטביוס', שמקורו בשם הלטיני 'אקטבוס', שהוא משותף לשם 'אקטאבון' העברי, שמקורו בתוספת 'א' למילה העברית עקב, שפירושה 'אח', 'אחד' או 'אחי'. בהתבסס על תרגום השבעים, "עקב" מתייחס לאחד, האחר, או האחי. בתקופה הרומאית, 'אקטבוס' היה שם שכבד, שהוענק לאנשים עשירים, שלא ניהלו עסקים. בימי הביניים, 'אקטביאן' היה שם של קהילות יהודיות, שהתכנסו בערים רבות. השם 'אקטביאן' נזכר גם בברית החדשה, במסכת 'אקטביאן' של יוחנן, שמסכת זו נחשבת אחת הספרים החשובים בברית החדשה.

in_greek.name: Οκταβιανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Οκταβιανός είναι η ελληνική εκδοχή του ονόματος Λατινικής καταγωγής 'Octavius', του οποίου η αρχική ετυμολογία προέρχεται από το Λατινικό 'Octavus', που είναι παρόμοιο με το ελληνικό όνομα 'Οκταβίνος', το οποίο ανήκει στην ομάδα των ονομάτων 'Οκταβ-'. Οι πηγές υποστηρίζουν ότι το όνομα 'Οκταβιανός' σχετίζεται με τον αριθμό οκτώ, που συμβολίζει την πνευματικότητα και τη σοφία. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα 'Οκταβιανός' αναφέρεται σε ένα άτομο, που απεικονίζεται με την ιδιότητα του 'Συναangelou'.

in_latin.name: Octavion
in_latin.long_meaning: Octavion est forma Latina nominis Graeci 'Octavianos', cuius origo est a forma Latina 'Octavius', quae est communis cum nomine Latino 'Octavon', quod est coniunctum cum nomine Hebraico 'Qetavon', quod est additio 'Qet' ad verbum Hebraicum 'Qev', quod significat 'frater' vel 'vicinus'. In translatione Septuaginta, 'Qev' refertur ad fratrem, alterum, vel vicinum. In aetate Romana, 'Octavius' erat nomen dignum, quod erat datum hominibus divitis, qui non habebant negotia. In aetate mediaevali, 'Octavion' erat nomen communitatum Iudaeorum, quae congregabantur in urbibus multarum. Nomen 'Octavion' est etiam mentio in Novo Testamento, in evangelio Ioannis, quae est una ex libris sanctis Novi Testamenti.

in_english.name: Octavion
in_english.long_meaning: Octavion is a Latin name with roots in the Greek name 'Octavianos', which originated from the Latin name 'Octavius'. The Latin name 'Octavius' shares similarities with the Hebrew name 'Qetavon', which is derived from the addition of 'Qet' to the Hebrew word 'Qev', meaning 'brother', 'other', or 'neighbor'. In the Septuagint translation, 'Qev' refers to a brother, other, or neighbor. In Roman times, 'Octavius' was a dignified name given to wealthy individuals who did not engage in business. In medieval times, 'Octavion' was the name of Jewish communities that gathered in many cities. The name 'Octavion' is also mentioned in the New Testament, in the Gospel of John, which is one of the holy books of the New Testament.

data.cultural_impact: The name Octavion holds a rich and fascinating history rooted in Latin culture. Octavian (the full form) was the name of Octavius Caesar, who became Rome's first emperor, Augustus, in 27 BC. The influence of this name extends into various areas such as literature, art, and even music. In music, Austrian composer Johann Strauss II (1825-1899) composed a waltz titled "Octavian" in 1881, showcasing the enduring appeal of the name.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Octavion, derived from the Latin 'octavus' which means 'eighth', carries profound spiritual significance in Christian tradition. In the Scriptures, eight is a symbol of new beginnings and regeneration. When Jesus was crucified on the Cross, His side was pierced and from His side flowed water and blood, and the centuries-old promise to Abraham was fulfilled: 'I will make you the father of many nations.' (Genesis 17:5) From the side of the new beginning, Jesus promised a new and spiritual birth to mankind. Additionally, in the Book of Revelation, the seventh seal's thunderous sound ushered in seven new thunderheads, making it the eighth one. With Octavion, we are reminded of the power and promise that a new beginning holds: hope, rebirth, and sustaining love.

historical_references.reference: Octavian, later known as Octavianus Augustus, was a Roman general and politician from the late Republican period who rose to power after the civil wars following the death of Julius Caesar. He played a decisive role in the events that led to the establishment of the Roman Empire and was the first Roman Emperor.

Octavian was born Gaius Octavius Thurinus in 63 BC in Velitrae, a town in the Roman province of Latium. After Caesar's assassination in 44 BC, Octavian was adopted as Caesar's heir and was given his name and the cognomen Augustus.

Lastly, in the business world, Octavion is a surname or given name that signifies leadership, ambition, and innovation, making it a popular choice among entrepreneurs on LinkedIn.
